problem: θ = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) gives the correct angle from the +x axis only when R_x > 0. With R_x < 0 the inverse tangent returns a first-quadrant angle, so the stated direction is wrong for forces pointing into the second or third quadrant.
fix: Add the quadrant rule: θ = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) measured from +x when R_x > 0; when R_x < 0 add 180° to the inverse-tangent value (or use θ = atan2(R_y, R_x)).

problem: The bullet says a wrench appears when R is parallel to M_O. That is only the special case. After the perpendicular part of M_O is cancelled, any system with R ≠ 0 and R·M_O ≠ 0 is a wrench, with the leftover couple being the component of M_O along R, which need not equal M_O itself.
fix: Write: R ≠ 0 and R·M_O ≠ 0: a wrench, meaning the force R plus the couple (R·M_O/|R|²)R along its own line; the case R parallel to M_O is the simplest example.

problem: The chain 'M_O = Σ M_O = Σ (r × F)' defines the total moment using the same symbol for the total and for each individual term, so a student cannot tell what is being summed.
fix: Write M_O = Σ (r_i × F_i) = Σ M_Oi, where M_Oi is the moment of force i about O.
